docs.title: Chest X-Ray Classification

docs.title: Protocol and reuse
docs.text:
The original Kaggle test fold contains 624 images. Filename-based pneumonia subtypes produce 242 bacterial, 234 normal and 148 viral labels. File hashes, model identity and prediction arrays accompany the replay. Historical checkpoint training membership and patient-level independence are not established by the old run records; clinical validation has not been performed.

Evaluation contract · Component licenses · Project guide · Limitations

docs.title: Benchmarks
docs.text: All numbers are on the held-out Kaggle test split (n=624). Hardware: RTX 3080 10 GB. Inference is single-image, FP32, no batching.

docs.title: Main results
docs.text: Model Accuracy Macro F1 AUROC Params Inference (ms/img, RTX 3080) ConvNeXt-V2-Tiny (ours, main) 91.3% 90.3% 97.5% ~28 M ~8 ms DINOv2 ViT-S linear probe (ours, baseline) 85.6% 84.2% 94.2% ~22 M ~12 ms

docs.title: Literature context
docs.text:
Widely reported numbers on the same Kaggle Pneumonia split, with the caveat that test-set definitions and augmentation vary between papers:

Model Accuracy Source ResNet-50 fine-tuned ~88.0% Rajpurkar et al., 2017 (CheXNet-style setup) DenseNet-121 ~89.5% Published replications 2018-2021 EfficientNet-B0 ~90.0% Published replications 2020-2022 ConvNeXt-V2-Tiny (ours) 91.3% This repo, v0.1.0

Our main model is competitive with the best reported numbers while being trained end-to-end on a single RTX 3080 in under 90 minutes with a 20-epoch budget.

docs.title: Trade-offs
docs.text:
• Main vs baseline (ConvNeXt-V2 vs DINOv2 linear probe): the baseline is a deliberate "how far do frozen features get us" reference. It's 6pp behind on accuracy but trains in under 10 minutes - useful as a sanity benchmark whenever you re-do the main training.
  • ConvNeXt-V2 vs ViT: ConvNeXt-V2-Tiny is ~28M params vs a comparable ViT-S's ~22M, but the convolutional inductive bias helps on small (~5k-image) datasets like this one. We tested both; ConvNeXt-V2 wins by ~2pp.
  • Why not an ensemble: a 2-3 model ensemble reliably adds ~1-2pp on this dataset, but at 2-3x inference cost - not worth it for a portfolio deployment story. If you need to push accuracy past 93%, start there.

docs.title: Reproducing these numbers
docs.text: See REPRODUCIBILITY.md for the one-command re-run. Expected variation: ± 0.5% from floating-point noise across CUDA driver versions.

docs.title: Original-source replay and preprocessing
docs.text:
The original Kaggle chest X-ray archive was retrieved on 2026-10-15: dataset 17810/version23812, 2,463,365,435 bytes, SHA256 f569fe885b0f921e836f3d6bcc8d7b3442f5e0ca4db4533d06b8cf25d2114ea1.

It contains two identical test trees and a separate __MACOSX metadata tree. Corresponding image bytes in the two normal test trees were compared; one 624-image cohort was used. The test manifest records every filename, derived class and SHA256. Its canonical records SHA256 is c763fd1a0cee678815db830f59c54164d57e82b16df6c630c4d1a8a4bdc14280.

Source receipt · Test manifest · Full native replay

docs.title: What was verified
docs.text:
The published native weights reproduce every cell of the committed main confusion matrix and the stored accuracy, macro-F1 and macro-AUROC. Model class ordering remains bacterial / normal / viral. An explicit alternative-order audit rejected the sample-driven swapped-label hypothesis; no labels were relabeled to improve results.

The baseline report is retained separately. Its checkpoint is not in this Hub snapshot, so a baseline replay is unavailable. The original test fold is reconstructed and hashed; historical training membership and patient-level independence were not recorded and are not inferred from an image-level replay.

docs.title: Exact preprocessing
docs.text:
Production evaluation applies RGB conversion, uint8 tensor bilinear resize to shortest edge 255 with antialiasing, torchvision CenterCrop(224), float32 rescaling 1/255, and ImageNet mean/std normalization.

The old native processor specified resize 256 and bicubic interpolation. A config-only 255/bilinear correction still differed: Transformers truncates the center anchor, while torchvision rounds it. data/hf_processor.py overrides only that crop method with torchvision's implementation. The exported native processor carries this small MIT-licensed module and its license notice.

Tensor tests cover square/nonsquare inputs and every committed sample. Real prediction comparisons cover all 624 original test images: zero differing top-1 predictions, identical confusion matrix and AUROC, maximum softmax-score difference 1.67e-6. Complete parity receipt.

The explicit torchvision recipe in the README requires no downloaded processor code. Loading the custom native processor through AutoImageProcessor requires reviewing its pinned module and passing trust_remote_code=True; native model weights continue to load with safetensors and trust_remote_code=False.

docs.title: Repeat the run
docs.text:
Use one unpacked chest_xray/ directory, preserving its original train/val/test folders. Preparation derives bacterial/viral classes from the filename suffixes.

uv sync --all-groups
uv run python -m chest_xray_classifier.data.prepare --raw /path/to/chest_xray --out data/processed
uv run python -m chest_xray_classifier.evaluation.evaluate \
  --hf-model kiselyovd/chest-xray-classifier \
  --revision d0de246d324b8b1a45523cd4b0a0a514a4aa7d89 \
  --weights-sha256 d3c0b8fba6caa340cfbabf06119c6a9988b018c277a72d9565e0f62acda2a7d0 \
  --out reports/replay-native.json

The evaluator rejects changed files or test membership before loading the model, then records class ordering, preprocessing, package/source identities, probabilities, labels and an array-file SHA256. Plot generation checks exact confusion counts and bounded AUROC drift and includes both correct and incorrect cases.

docs.title: Limitations & Failure Modes
docs.text: This page is a deliberate call-out of where the published model falls short. Read it before using the weights for anything beyond demo / research.

docs.title: Dataset scope
docs.text:
• Pediatric population bias: the Kaggle Chest X-Ray Pneumonia set (Kermany et al., 2018) is sourced from a pediatric cohort (Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center). Adult X-rays - different cardiothoracic ratio, bone density, calcifications - are out of distribution; expect accuracy to drop on them.
  • Single-institution sourcing: All 5856 images come from one hospital's imaging pipeline. Scanner model, acquisition protocol, and post-processing differ across institutions and will shift the input distribution.
  • Small held-out test set: 624 test images. Reported 91.3% accuracy has a ~±1.5% confidence interval - don't over-interpret fractional gains.

docs.title: Class boundaries
docs.text:
• Bacterial vs viral pneumonia: these classes overlap in radiographic appearance; even experienced radiologists disagree in a meaningful fraction of cases. The model's per-class recall reflects this - viral recall is ~3pp lower than normal.
  • Only 3 classes: Normal / Bacterial / Viral. Real clinical chest X-rays contain many other findings (TB, lung cancer, COVID-19, pneumothorax, pleural effusion) that the model has never seen. Any prediction on such an input is spurious.

docs.title: Known failure modes
docs.text:
• Heavy infiltrate patterns (whiteout consolidation) get predicted as bacterial pneumonia regardless of etiology.
  • Grid-like artifacts from bedside portable radiographs sometimes trigger false-positive classifications.
  • Low-contrast or underexposed films degrade performance sharply - no automatic contrast normalisation is applied beyond standard ImageNet mean/std.
  • Lateral views were not in the training set; the model will confidently mis-classify them.

docs.title: Adversarial & reliability
docs.text:
• No adversarial robustness testing has been performed. The model is trained on clean images only.
  • No uncertainty estimation - the model outputs a single softmax probability. For clinical use you'd want calibrated confidence or an ensemble.

docs.title: Not a medical device
docs.text:
• This model is not FDA-cleared, CE-marked, or clinically validated. It is a computer-vision portfolio project.
  • Any use beyond research / educational demos requires independent clinical validation by qualified professionals.

docs.title: What this project is good for
docs.text:
• Demonstrating a production ML pipeline: Hydra configs, Lightning training loop, FastAPI serving, Docker/CI/CD, HuggingFace Hub distribution.
  • A reproducible baseline others can fork and extend with better data, calibration, and explainability.
  • Comparing ConvNeXt-V2 vs DINOv2 on a small chest-X-ray dataset with a deliberately modest training budget.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: This project is designed to produce identical results across re-runs on the same hardware. Here's how each moving part is pinned.

docs.title: Random seeds
docs.text:
• seed: 42 in configs/config.yaml is threaded through seed_everything() at the start of src/chest_xray_classifier/training/train.py.
  • Lightning's deterministic="warn" mode is set on the Trainer - non-deterministic CUDA ops (if any) emit a warning rather than silently using a non-deterministic impl.
  • Data split is deterministic via configs/data/default.yaml:val_split=0.1 + seed: ${seed}.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• pyproject.toml declares direct deps; uv.lock is committed to git and pins every transitive package version + hash.
  • .python-version = 3.13 - interpreters in CI and local dev must match.
  • CUDA torch pinned via [[tool.uv.index]] pytorch-cu124 on Win/Linux; re-pinning to a different CUDA requires a lockfile regen.
  • CI runs the suite against Python 3.12 + 3.13 via a matrix strategy so regressions are caught in both.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
• data/sample/ (8 images + labels) is in git - CI + smoke tests work without any external download.
  • data/raw/ and data/processed/ are DVC-tracked (see dvc.yaml). DVC remote is local-only by default; configure one for team use.
  • Kaggle source: the Chest X-Ray Pneumonia dataset is pre-split (train / val / test) - no custom splitting, so splits are deterministic across machines.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
• Dockerfile is multi-stage (base, training, serving); .dockerignore keeps build context minimal.
  • Published images live at ghcr.io/kiselyovd/chest-xray-classifier:<tag>; SHA256 digests are visible on the GHCR web UI.
  • Base image: python:3.13-slim-bookworm - Debian package versions roll with Debian security updates but the Python version itself is frozen.

docs.title: Model weights
docs.text:
• Published to HuggingFace Hub under kiselyovd/chest-xray-classifier. Each release tag (e.g. v0.1.0) corresponds to a specific HF commit SHA visible in the repo's git log on huggingface.co.
  • Weights ship as model.safetensors - a safe, reproducible binary format.

Generic image dataset with class-subdir layout.

Source code in src/chest_xray_classifier/data/dataset.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    root: Path | str,
    transform: Callable | None = None,
    extensions: tuple[str, ...] = (".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".tif", ".tiff"),
) -> None:
    self.root = Path(root)
    self.transform = transform
    self.samples: list[tuple[Path, int]] = []
    classes = sorted(p.name for p in self.root.iterdir() if p.is_dir())
    self.class_to_idx = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(classes)}
    for cls, idx in self.class_to_idx.items():
        for ext in extensions:
            self.samples.extend((p, idx) for p in (self.root / cls).glob(f"**/*{ext}"))

build_hf_processor(image_size: int = 224)

Match the actual evaluation resize, crop and normalization in a native processor.

Source code in src/chest_xray_classifier/data/transforms.py 
def build_hf_processor(image_size: int = 224):
    """Match the actual evaluation resize, crop and normalization in a native processor."""
    from .hf_processor import ChestXrayImageProcessor

    if image_size != 224:
        raise ValueError("The published native export contract is validated for 224px crops")
    resize_edge = int(image_size * 1.14)
    return ChestXrayImageProcessor(
        size={"shortest_edge": image_size},
        crop_pct=image_size / resize_edge,
        resample=2,
        do_convert_rgb=True,
        do_rescale=True,
        rescale_factor=1 / 255,
        do_normalize=True,
        image_mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406],
        image_std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225],
    )

docs.title: verify_test_data
docs.text:
verify_test_data(root: Path, manifest_path: Path) -> dict

Require exact original test membership and file contents before inference.

Source code in src/chest_xray_classifier/evaluation/evaluate.py 
def verify_test_data(root: Path, manifest_path: Path) -> dict:
    """Require exact original test membership and file contents before inference."""
    manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    serialized = json.dumps(manifest["records"], sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
    if hashlib.sha256(serialized.encode()).hexdigest() != manifest["records_sha256"]:
        raise ValueError("Test manifest content hash mismatch")
    expected = {r["image"] for r in manifest["records"]}
    if len(expected) != len(manifest["records"]) or len(expected) != manifest["count"]:
        raise ValueError("Test manifest contains duplicate or inconsistent records")
    actual = {p.relative_to(root).as_posix() for p in root.rglob("*") if p.is_file()}
    if actual != expected:
        raise ValueError("Test image membership differs from manifest")
    for record in manifest["records"]:
        if record["class"] not in CLASSES or Path(record["image"]).parts[0] != record["class"]:
            raise ValueError("Test record label differs from its class directory")
        path = (root / record["image"]).resolve()
        if not path.is_relative_to(root.resolve()):
            raise ValueError("Test manifest path escapes data directory")
        if file_sha256(path) != record["sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("Test image content hash mismatch")
    log.info("evaluation.cohort_verified", images=len(expected), hash=manifest["records_sha256"])
    return manifest

load_model(checkpoint_path: str | Path)

Load a Lightning module from checkpoint, rebuilding the backbone from hparams.

Source code in src/chest_xray_classifier/inference/predict.py 
def load_model(checkpoint_path: str | Path):
    """Load a Lightning module from checkpoint, rebuilding the backbone from hparams."""
    import torch

    from ..models import ClassificationModule, build_model

    ckpt = torch.load(str(checkpoint_path), map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
    hp = ckpt.get("hyper_parameters", {})
    model_name = hp.get("model_name")
    num_classes = hp.get("num_classes")
    if model_name is None or num_classes is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "Checkpoint missing model_name/num_classes hparams - "
            "re-train after upgrading ClassificationModule."
        )
    backbone = build_model(model_name, num_classes=num_classes, pretrained=False)
    return ClassificationModule.load_from_checkpoint(str(checkpoint_path), model=backbone)

docs.title: predict
docs.text:
predict(model, input_path: str | Path)

Run a single prediction. Returns a task-specific result dict.

Source code in src/chest_xray_classifier/inference/predict.py 
def predict(model, input_path: str | Path):
    """Run a single prediction. Returns a task-specific result dict."""
    import torch
    from PIL import Image

    from ..data.transforms import build_eval_transforms

    model.eval()
    tf = build_eval_transforms()
    img = Image.open(input_path).convert("RGB")
    x = tf(img).unsqueeze(0)
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits = model._forward_logits(x) if hasattr(model, "_forward_logits") else model(x)
        probs = logits.softmax(-1).squeeze(0).tolist()
    return {"probs": probs, "pred": int(max(range(len(probs)), key=probs.__getitem__))}

docs.title: Model choices
docs.text:
• Main - ConvNeXt-V2-Tiny. Modern CNN with strong ImageNet-22k pretraining; good accuracy/compute balance for medical imaging. Pre-trained via transformers.ConvNextV2ForImageClassification with a 3-label classification head.
  • Baseline - DINOv2 ViT-S linear probe. Frozen self-supervised backbone (facebook/dinov2-small) with a single trainable linear layer on top of the [CLS] embedding. Acts as a methodology sanity check - the main model must clearly beat a frozen generic feature extractor to justify the compute.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Metric Why Per-class precision/recall/F1 Detect class-specific weakness (viral is the hardest + smallest class) Macro F1 Headline number tolerant of class imbalance Confusion matrix Expose bacterial↔viral confusions (clinically meaningful) Macro AUROC (OvR) Threshold-independent separability, averaged over classes

Accuracy alone is avoided - bacterial_pneumonia dominates the train split.

docs.title: Key conventions
docs.text:
• Class index order is alphabetical, matching torchvision.ImageFolder: ("bacterial_pneumonia", "normal", "viral_pneumonia").
  • Checkpoint contains model_name in its hyperparameters so inference.load_model can rebuild the backbone without metadata supplied by the caller.
  • Lightning trainer seed-controlled via Hydra seed; deterministic mode on.

docs.title: Dataset
docs.text:
Paul Mooney's Chest X-Ray Images (Pneumonia) on Kaggle - 5,856 pediatric frontal chest radiographs. The original layout has two classes (NORMAL, PNEUMONIA); src/chest_xray_classifier/data/prepare.py splits PNEUMONIA into bacterial_pneumonia and viral_pneumonia using the _bacteria_ / _virus_ substrings in the filenames, producing a three-class target space.

Resulting distribution (train + val + test): ~1,583 normal / 2,780 bacterial / 1,493 viral.

from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download

from chest_xray_classifier.inference.predict import load_model, predict

ckpt_dir = snapshot_download("kiselyovd/chest-xray-classifier")
model = load_model(f"{ckpt_dir}/best.ckpt")
result = predict(model, "path/to/radiograph.jpeg")
# {"pred": 1, "probs": [0.02, 0.95, 0.03]}

Class index order: ("bacterial_pneumonia", "normal", "viral_pneumonia").

docs.title: Inside the chest X-ray test reports
docs.text:
Explore the stored test reports for ConvNeXt-V2 and the DINOv2 baseline. Choose a model, inspect a true class, and select a matrix cell to see what the count means.

The main model's stored evaluation report. Explore the example

Use the controls to inspect this project's published artifacts.

The source example is available above; interactive controls load when JavaScript is enabled.

docs.title: Reading the result
docs.text:
Both reports use 624 test radiographs and the same three dataset classes. The main model records 54 classification errors; the baseline records 90. The matrix counts and per-class precision, recall, and F1 are read from committed JSON, rather than extracted from a chart.

The images in the gallery are committed smoke examples with dataset labels. They are separate from the aggregate test report; the stored reports do not include per-image predictions or scores for them.

This is a research and educational benchmark on pediatric chest radiographs. It is not clinical validation. Evaluation protocol and limitations.

docs.title: Inspect actual correct predictions and errors
docs.text:
These are actual outputs from the pinned native model on the original 624-image test fold. The selection includes the median-score correct example and highest-score error for each true class. It is an illustration of model behavior, not a second benchmark or a balanced estimate of error frequency. Scores are uncalibrated softmax values.
